prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset type: a single fine-line architectural illustration for the Chinese heritage collection 访古. Image 1 is STYLE ONLY, the Vairocana Buddha contour master. Match the master's elegant delicate slightly organic thin black strokes, sparse detail and broad empty white surfaces. Image 2 is SUBJECT GEOMETRY: the actual Central Buddha Hall 中佛殿 at Chongming Temple 崇明寺, Guojiazhuang village, Gaoping, Shanxi. Image 3 is its side view to confirm the deep eaves and large bracket stacks. Draw ONLY this small Northern Song hall from image2, exactly THREE bays with a plain central double doorway between TWO rectangular vertical-bar windows, squat largely solid wall body, broad HUGE overhanging shallow hipped-gable roof (歇山) on massive tall layered dougong bracket sets. Preserve the distinction between the short wall-embedded main columns and the TWO very thin later eave support posts at the far left and far right outside the wall; do not invent an open central colonnade or extra doors. Retain the broad bracket-layer silhouette, very low flat roof pitch, raised ridge beasts at either end and small central ridge finial. Keep roof broad and sweeping as photo, not steep and not a palace. A simple low stone terrace with a modest central short stair. Remove ALL foreground stone steles including the large square one at the right and the little one beside the entrance; don't mistake them for columns. Remove side buildings, lanterns, couplets, plaques, people, debris, foliage, wires, paving texture and sky. Straighten low wide-angle perspective into a calm near-frontal elevation, verticals vertical. BLACK INK ON PURE WHITE. Fine outline-only contours, sparing internal structural lines. All walls, roof, windows and eave undersides remain WHITE, no filled shadows, no grey shading, crosshatching, dense brick grid or texture. Only a few spaced roof-direction strokes, selected simple curls for carved ornament. No calligraphy, letters, measurements, labels, arrows, watermark, frame or borders. Landscape1536x1024, complete building with roof corners and plinth fully within 82% canvas width and generous margins. It should look drawn by the same hand as the Buddha master, retaining actual architectural identity.
